chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ajlan Abu Salih, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Set me upon the limits of faith.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony that there is no god except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and the acknowledgement of what he brought from Allah, and the five prayers, and the payment of zakat, and fasting the month of Ramadan, and the pilgrimage to the House, and the Wilayah of our Wali and the enmity of our enemies, and entering with the truthful.'
ai.seo_question: What are the complete pillars of faith in Shia Islam according to the hadith of Abu Abdillah?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi expands the traditional five pillars of Islam by integrating 'Wilayah' (authority of the Imams) and 'Ala' al-Adaw' (enmity of their enemies) as essential components of Iman, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the inseparability of belief and allegiance. It underscores the doctrinal concept of 'Al-Dukhul ma'a al-Sadiqin' (entering with the truthful), linking personal piety to the cosmic hierarchy of the Ahl al-Bayt. This holistic view positions the Imam not merely as a political leader but as the spiritual axis of faith required for the validity of ritual worship.
